item.title: “The Built Metaphor” films by Robert Beavers and Ute Aurand — Mon Oct 5, 6:30 PM — Innis Town Hall
item.description:
Join Ute Aurand and Robert Beavers in person for a two-day program of screenings and discussion exploring affinities between cinema and architecture through their work.
Partners of twenty years and two of experimental cinema's most distinctive voices, Aurand and Beavers have rarely had their films presented in dialogue. "The Built Metaphor" (Oct. 5) focuses on urban architectural space, ornament and construction.
“The Built Metaphor” will be followed by a panel discussion with the filmmakers, Claire Zimmerman and Robert Levit.

item.title: Murder Mystery Double Book Launch — Tue Oct 6, 5:00 PM — Ben McNally Books
item.description: [at Ben McNally Books] Join us at Ben McNally Books, as we celebrate the launches of two murder mysteries: A Killing Cold by Alice Fitzpatrick, and Murder by Nordic Design by A.L. Jensen About the Books: A Killing Cold THE THIRD BOOK IN THE MEREDITH ISLAND MYSTERIES It’s Christmas on Meredith Island, and Kate Galway is looking forward to spending some mother-daughter time with her barrister daughter, Alex. But Kate is forced to adjust her plans when Alex arrives accompanied by her father, Detective Chief Inspector James Hewitt, Kate’s ex-husband. The island’s matriarch, Sophie Sutherland, is eager to reunite with her old beau, Teddy Bartell, who shows up with an entourage of relations, including his son, the son’s abrasive second wife, and her twin brother. Everyone joins in the Christmas celebrations at the pub, but the party comes to an abrupt end when someone ingests a lethal dose of cyanide. A winter storm has shut down access to the mainland, trapping the killer on the island.

item.title: The Blackhurst Project: Inhabitants of the Deep — Thu Oct 8, 6:00 PM — Blackhurst Cultural Centre
item.description:
The Blackhurst Project, a new monthly literary series from Blackhurst Cultural Centre, launches with Jonathan Howard in conversation with I. Augustus Durham.
Jonathan Howard, Assistant Professor of English and Black Studies at Yale University and author of Inhabitants of the Deep: The Blueness of Blackness, joins I. Augustus Durham, Assistant Professor of English at the University of Toronto and author of Stay Black and Die: On Melancholy and Genius, for an evening of Black literature, scholarship and conversation.
In Inhabitants of the Deep, Howard undertakes a Black ecocritical study of the “deep”, encompassing oceans, rivers, lakes and the notion of depth itself, and its place within African American literature and expressive culture. item.title: Prompt Engineering con Copilot: construye prompts que realmente funcionen — Fri Oct 9, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto ¿Utilizas Copilot pero no siempre obtienes los resultados que esperas?
En esta sesión práctica aprenderemos a dejar de improvisar prompts y construiremos juntos un framework sencillo para crear instrucciones más claras, efectivas y reutilizables con Microsoft Copilot.
Trabajaremos con seis elementos: contexto, objetivo, información, restricciones, resultado esperado y criterios de evaluación. A través de ejemplos y demostraciones en vivo, transformaremos prompts simples en instrucciones estructuradas que los participantes podrán reutilizar y adaptar a situaciones reales.
El objetivo no es memorizar “el prompt perfecto”, sino aprender una metodología que permita diseñar, probar y mejorar nuestros propios prompts.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

item.title: 🍁 Fall Walk: Finch Recreational Trail & Park Adventure! 🌾🚶‍♂️ (16KM) — Sat Oct 10, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 🍁 Fall Walk: Finch Recreational Trail & Park Adventure! 🌾
### An Easy, Flat Fall Walk Through Toronto's Green Spaces
Looking for an easy way to enjoy the fall colours without tackling a difficult hike? Join us for a relaxed walk from **Pioneer Village Station to Finch Station**, travelling through Black Creek Parkland and along the **Finch Recreational Trail**.
This is one of our members' favourite walks for a reason. The route is mostly flat and takes us through open fields, wooded areas, and quiet green spaces that feel surprisingly far removed from the city.
We'll take our time, enjoy the changing leaves, stop for a break by **Dufferin Creek**, and spend the day walking and getting to know each other.
